_READ_THIS_FIRST: ############ EXAMPLE FILE - NOT A MANIFEST - DO NOT DEPLOY ############ This file exists ONLY to document the shape of data/bitcoin-puppets-mainnet.json. Every value below is a self-identifying placeholder. The first 16 bytes of every inscriptionTxid are the ASCII string "EXAMPLE-NOT-REAL", so none of these identities can exist on Bitcoin. No real Bitcoin Puppets inscription id appears in this repository, and none ever should be invented.
_HOW_TO_PRODUCE_THE_REAL_FILE: Source the canonical Bitcoin Puppets inscription set yourself, from an indexer you operate or independently trust, and have at least two people reconcile it against a second independent index before it is used. Save it as data/bitcoin-puppets-mainnet.json. That file is intentionally NOT committed here: committing it would make an unreviewed list look blessed by the repository.
_FAIL_CLOSED: The manifest builder MUST refuse to run when data/bitcoin-puppets-mainnet.json is missing, and MUST NOT fall back to this example. PuppetCollectionRegistry takes its Merkle root as an immutable constructor argument, so a deployment without a verified manifest either does not happen or permanently commits to a wrong root. There is no setter and no upgrade path that can repair it afterwards.
_CANONICAL_MEANS: "Canonical" means canonical to this protocol deployment. It is not an endorsement, affiliation or approval claim by the Bitcoin Puppets project, and it must never be presented as one.
_TRUST_BOUNDARY: This registry answers membership only. It never asserts who currently owns an inscription; Bitcoin facts are asserted by a 3-of-5 quorum of independent attestors elsewhere in the protocol. The original Bitcoin Puppet never leaves Bitcoin.
sourcedFrom: REPLACE-ME: indexer name, endpoint, snapshot height and the second index used to reconcile it
_derivedFieldsNote: merkleRoot, manifestHash and leafCount are OUTPUTS of the builder, not inputs. They are null here on purpose: a placeholder root that looked real is exactly the kind of value that gets copy-pasted into a deployment script.

entries._note: Shares its reveal transaction with the next entry. A reveal transaction can carry several inscriptions, so (txid, index) is the identity and txid alone is not.

entryRules.inscriptionTxid: Reveal transaction id in big-endian / RPC display order (the order a block explorer shows), lowercase 64-hex, 0x-prefixed, left-padded into bytes32. Byte order is a security primitive: the SDK, the Merkle builder, the attestors and Solidity must all agree.
entryRules.inscriptionIndex: Inscription index within that reveal transaction (the iN suffix). Non-negative and must fit uint32.
entryRules.uniqueness: The pair (inscriptionTxid, inscriptionIndex) must be unique across the whole file. The builder must reject duplicates rather than silently deduplicate them: a duplicate means the source list is wrong, and it also makes proof generation ambiguous.

algorithm.leafOrdering: sorted ascending as unsigned big-endian 256-bit integers; duplicates rejected
algorithm.oddNode: promoted unchanged to the next level; never self-paired
algorithm.reference: contracts/test/helpers/MerkleFixture.sol carries the same algorithm spelled out step by step, and data/test-fixtures/puppets-fixture-manifest.json carries executable golden vectors for it.
